'''Francisca Nneka Okeke''' {{Audio|LL-Q33578 (ibo)-Vivian Amalachukwu-Francisca Nneka Okeke.wav|Listen|help=no}} is a [[Nigerians|Nigerian]] [[physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unn.edu.ng/internals/staff/viewProfile/NTcw|access-date=2021-05-20|website=www.unn.edu.ng|title=UNN Staff Profile }}</ref> She is a [[professor]] of [[physics]] at the [[University of Nigeria, Nsukka]] and first female head of a department in the university.<ref>{{cite web|author=|url=http://atlantablackstar.com/2013/04/01/nigerian-female-professor-francisca-okeke-wins-100000-prize/ |title=Nigerian Female Professor Francisca Okeke Wins $100,000 Prize |publisher=Atlanta Black Star |date=2013-04-01 |accessdate=2013-05-09}}</ref> Due to her research in physics and space science, the [[International Astronomical Union]] (IAU) named Asteroid 149831 ''Okeke'' after Professor Okeke, in August, 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-09-09 |title=They named an asteroid after this Nigerian Professor - See why |url=https://www.pulse.ng/story/prof-francisca-okeke-2025090912000193085 |access-date=2026-07-19 |newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Rapheal |date=2025-10-11 |title=It’s exciting that global body named asteroid after me – Okeke, |url=https://thesun.ng/its-exciting-that-global-body-named-asteroid-after-me-okeke-professor-of-physics-unn/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|access-date=2026-07-19 |newspaper=[[The Sun (Nigeria)|The Sun]]|language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Francisca Okeke is from [[Idemili North]] in [[Anambra State]]. She earned a Bachelor of Science in physics (1980), a Master of Science in science education (1985), a [[Master of Science]] in applied Earth geophysics (1989), and a Ph.D. in ionospheric geophysics (1995), from the [[University of Nigeria]]. She carried out her postdoctoral work at the [[University of Tokyo]], [[Japan]].<ref name="nsesafoundation.org">{{Cite web|date=2019-07-20|title=Meet Professor Francisca Nneka Okeke, Professor of Physics, University of Nigeria, Nsukka, (UNN)|url=https://nsesafoundation.org/stem-wow-nneka/|access-date=2021-10-22|website=Nsesa Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref>

Okeke was the head of Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka from 2003 to 2006 and was the dean of the Faculty of Physical Sciences from 2008 to 2010.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.unn.edu.ng/internals/staff/viewProfile/NTcw|access-date=2021-05-18|website=www.unn.edu.ng|title=UNN Staff Profile }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Inspiring Youth: Francisca Nneka Okeke {{!}} United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/natural-sciences/special-themes/science-education/inspiring-youth/inspiring-youth-francisca-nneka-okeke/|access-date=2020-05-27|website=www.unesco.org}}</ref> She was the first woman to hold both positions.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Inspiring Youth: Francisca Nneka Okeke {{!}} United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/natural-sciences/special-themes/science-education/inspiring-youth/inspiring-youth-francisca-nneka-okeke/|access-date=2019-05-08|website=www.unesco.org}}</ref> Additionally, Okeke was the first female professor of physics in the eastern part of Nigeria.<ref name="nsesafoundation.org"/> During her time as head of department, she advocated for inclusion of more women in the department, which led to the hiring of three new female faculty members and as dean of the faculty she prioritised employing women in faculty positions in the physical sciences. She advocates for the wider participation of women and girls in science and technology.<ref name=":1" />

In 2011, she was elected as [[List of fellows of the Nigerian Academy of Science|fellow of the Nigerian Academy of Science]], the highest scientific organization in Nigeria. She was inducted into the academy alongside [[Abba Gumel]], a professor of [[Mathematics|mathematical biology]] and fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/fellows-of-the-academy/ |title=Fellows of the academy |work=www.nas.org.ng |accessdate=September 15, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151109232120/http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/fellows-of-the-academy/ |archivedate=November 9, 2015 }}</ref>

==Scientific research==
Okeke has dedicated much of her career to studying the [[ionosphere]] and the "[[Equatorial electrojet|equatorial electrojet phenomenon]]."<ref name=":0" />

Okeke research on how solar activity in the [[ionosphere]] affects the Earth's magnetic field could lead to a better understanding of climate change and help pinpoint sources of dramatic phenomena like [[tsunamis]] and earthquakes.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.la-croix.com/Actualite/Monde/Francisca-Okeke-une-physicienne-fascinee-par-le-ciel-2013-04-01-927499 |title=Francisca Okeke, une physicienne fascinée par le ciel |newspaper=La Croix |language=fr |publisher=La-Croix.com |date= April 2013|accessdate=2013-05-09}}</ref>

She has successfully supervised 12 Ph.D. and about 28 M.Sc. students. In 2010, one of her Female PhD students, Theresa Obiekezie, won an AU-TWAS young scientist Award.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Recipients of AU-TWAS Awards|url=https://twas.org/recipients-au-twas-awards|access-date=2021-10-22|website=TWAS|language=en}}</ref>

==Awards==
Okeke was named [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science Awards]] Laureate for Africa and Arab States in 2013<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unesco.org/new/en/natural-sciences/special-themes/science-education/inspiring-youth/inspiring-youth-francisca-nneka-okeke/ |title=Inspiring Youth: Francisca Nneka Okeke &#124; United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization |publisher=Unesco.org |date=2012-10-05 |accessdate=2013-05-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.slateafrique.com/172165/nigeria-une-scientifique-remporte-le-prix-loreal-unesco |title=Nigeria : une scientifique remporte le prix L'OrĂŠal-Unesco |publisher=Slate Afrique |date=2013-04-19 |accessdate=2013-05-09}}</ref> for her significant contributions to the understanding of daily variations of the ion currents in the upper atmosphere which may further our understanding of climate change. She was cited as one of the Top 100 most influential Africans by [[New African]] magazine in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2013-12-12|title=Top 100 Influential People In Africa: See the Nigerian list|url=https://newsghana.com.gh/top-100-influential-people-in-africa-see-the-nigerian-list/|access-date=2021-01-06|website=News Ghana|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Okeke married a physicist, [[Pius Nwankwo Okeke]], at the age of 18, and they have six children.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-21 |title=From Idemili to the Stars: Prof. Francisca Nneka Okeke Honoured with Asteroid Naming |url=https://thenigeriaeducationnews.com/2025/08/21/from-idemili-to-the-stars-prof-francisca-nneka-okeke-honoured-with-asteroid-naming/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |website=Nigeria Education News |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Okoye |first1=Patrick N. |title=How A Notorious Physics Problem Led Prof Okeke To Physics |url=https://www.afriscitech.com/en/blogs/sci-com-nigeria/1019-how-a-notorious-physics-problem-led-prof-okeke-to-physics |website=Science Communication Hub Nigeria |publisher=Medium |access-date=16 March 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204104003/https://www.afriscitech.com/en/blogs/sci-com-nigeria/1019-how-a-notorious-physics-problem-led-prof-okeke-to-physics |archive-date=2023-12-04}}</ref>
